**THE v2 SHELL IMPLEMENTATION IS DELETED AT THE CUT, FAIL-FORWARD -- AND THAT IS 26 FILES, NOT THE `bin/` DIRECTORY.** **REWORDED 2026-08-30 (vc) ON hv's RULING, BECAUSE THE PARENTHETICAL WAS LOAD-BEARING AND WRONG.** The row read _the shell implementation (`bin/`) is pruned at the cut_, and read literally that deletes **v3's own build and delivery system**, which is bigger than the thing being removed:

    POPULATION A -- THE SUBJECT      26 files   12,415 lines   `bin/intent` + 25 `bin/intent_*`
    POPULATION B -- MUST SURVIVE     57 files   ~18,300 lines  `bin/int`, `bin/devbin`, `bin/.devbin/`

**`bin/devbin build all` is the ONLY door that produces a coherent binary pair** (`restart.md`: _a build is the delivery_; it deletes both binaries to force the provenance embeds and verifies them as a SET, which is why a bare `cargo build --release` is not the door). **A criterion whose plain reading deletes the release system is not a stricter criterion, it is a wrong one.**

**THE DELETION IS BLOCKED ON FOUR CALL SITES AND THEY ARE ALL IN ONE FILE -- `bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release`, WHICH IS THE RELEASE SCRIPT ITSELF.** Measured 2026-08-30:

    :67   HELPERS="$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/intent_helpers"                        sources v2
    :373  "$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/intent" doctor                                 abort-on-failure
    :663  "$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/intent" agents sync                            abort-on-failure
    :690  "$PROJECT_ROOT/bin/intent" claude upgrade --apply --skip-settings abort-on-failure

**So the script that ships v3 invokes v2 three times, and deleting the subject breaks the release in which it is deleted.** That is the whole of why this row is not a sweep.

**THREE OF THE FOUR PORT STRAIGHT ACROSS. THE FOURTH IS A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE THAT TURNS OUT TO BE SAFE, AND A TEST LANDED HOURS EARLIER IS WHY.** v3's `claude upgrade` carries `--apply` and `--force` and **has no `--skip-settings`**, so the port rewrites `.claude/settings.json` on every release where v2 declined to. **That is a no-op rather than a risk, and it is ASSERTED rather than assumed:** `no_pm_state_in_output.rs` (dc, `a29f04ec`) drives that `settings.json` needs no substitution and is byte-identical to its template, so regenerating it writes the same bytes. **RULED: port to `--apply` and keep the arm that makes it safe.**

**WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS: any `bin/intent*` file of population A surviving the cut; any population B file deleted with it; or a release path that still executes v2.**
